title: BMW X5 vs Audi Q7: Which Used Luxury SUV Is Better?
html:
The BMW X5 and Audi Q7 are both premium SUVs, but they suit slightly different buyers. The BMW X5 is worth considering if you prioritise driving enjoyment and a driver-focused cabin. The Audi Q7 is a strong option for families who need flexible seating and a spacious interior.

The right choice depends on the specific vehicle, not just the badge. Engine, model year, specification, service history and condition can all affect running costs and reliability.

If you are buying either SUV second-hand, compare the following before making a decision:

  • Passenger and luggage space for your everyday needs.
  • Fuel economy, insurance and routine maintenance costs.
  • Service history and any previous mechanical or electrical faults.
  • The results of an independent inspection and diagnostic check.
  • Whether the vehicle qualifies for an extended warranty and what that policy actually covers.

Both vehicles can be expensive to repair when complex components fail. A careful inspection and realistic ownership budget are more useful than assuming one model is automatically more reliable than the other.

BMW X5 vs Audi Q7: Key Differences at a Glance

FeatureBMW X5Audi Q7
Main appealDriver-focused luxury and responsive handlingFamily practicality and passenger flexibility
SeatingCommonly five seats; a third row is available on selected versionsSeven-seat layouts are available; check the exact vehicle
Driving experienceOften appeals to drivers who enjoy a more engaging feelOften appeals to drivers who prioritise comfort and refinement
Four-wheel drivexDrive on applicable versionsquattro on applicable versions
Interior technologyBMW iDrive and equipment that varies by model yearAudi MMI and equipment that varies by model year
Areas to inspectDrivetrain, suspension, cooling and electronics, depending on versionSuspension, gearbox, emissions systems and electronics, depending on version
Best fitDrivers who want a premium SUV with a sporty characterFamilies who value space and seating flexibility

These are general differences, not a substitute for checking the specification of an individual car. Equipment, seating, boot capacity and mechanical systems vary by year, trim and engine.

1. Audi Q7 vs BMW X5: Which Is Better for Families?

Audi Q7: Space and seating flexibility

The Audi Q7 deserves a place on your shortlist if you regularly carry several passengers or need the option of a third row.

Before buying, check whether the particular vehicle has seven seats and whether the layout works for your family. Consider how easy it is to access the rear seats, how much luggage space remains with all seats in use, and whether child seats fit the way you need them to.

Also test the practical details that are easy to overlook during a quick viewing:

  • Rear-seat legroom and headroom.
  • Boot access and folding-seat operation.
  • ISOFIX positions and child-seat compatibility.
  • Visibility, parking sensors and camera systems.
  • The operation of powered seats, tailgate and other electrical features.

The Q7 may be the more practical choice for a family that frequently needs extra seats, but its larger dimensions may not suit every driveway or parking space.

BMW X5: Comfort for everyday driving

The BMW X5 is worth considering if you want a premium SUV for commuting, school runs, motorway journeys and family trips, without necessarily needing seven seats.

Its appeal lies in combining a luxury interior with a driving experience that many buyers find engaging. However, the precise ride, handling and equipment depend on the version, wheel size, suspension and optional features.

During a test drive, pay attention to low-speed comfort, visibility, steering, parking convenience and rear-seat space. Test every major electrical feature rather than assuming it works because the vehicle looks well maintained.

Family verdict: Consider the Q7 first if seven-seat flexibility is a regular requirement. The X5 may be the better fit if five seats are sufficient and you prefer its driving character.

2. BMW X5 vs Audi Q7: Running Costs in the UK

The purchase price is only part of the cost of owning a used luxury SUV. Your budget should also account for fuel, insurance, servicing, tyres, brakes and unexpected repairs.

Neither model is automatically cheaper to run in every configuration. A petrol X5, a diesel X5 and different Q7 engine options can have very different costs. Vehicle age, annual mileage, driving conditions and maintenance history matter too.

Ownership costWhat to compare
FuelOfficial economy figures for the exact engine and model year
InsuranceQuotes using the vehicle's registration and your circumstances
ServicingManufacturer schedule and local garage estimates
TyresSize, brand and replacement cost
BrakesParts and labour estimates for the exact version
RepairsInspection findings and known issues relevant to that engine
WarrantyPremium, claim limit, excess, covered components and exclusions

How to compare fuel economy properly

Do not rely on one MPG figure for every BMW X5 or Audi Q7. Published figures can vary by engine, trim and testing standard, while real-world consumption depends on driving style and conditions.

Look up the official figures for the exact versions you are comparing. Then consider your own driving pattern. Frequent short journeys, motorway commuting and towing can lead to different fuel costs.

Do not overlook depreciation and insurance

Two similarly priced SUVs can have different insurance premiums, service requirements and resale prospects. Obtain insurance quotes before buying and consider the vehicle's age, mileage, condition and expected ownership period.

Practical tip: Build an annual ownership budget before choosing between the two. Include routine expenses and leave room for an unexpected repair, even if you decide to buy a warranty.

3. Common BMW X5 and Audi Q7 Repair Risks

Both vehicles use complex mechanical, electronic and driver-assistance systems. Their repair risks vary by generation, engine and equipment, so a used-car inspection should focus on the actual vehicle rather than a generic list of faults.

The following are areas worth checking, not a claim that every vehicle will develop these problems.

BMW X5: What should you inspect?

1. Drivetrain and xDrive system

On applicable four-wheel-drive versions, investigate shuddering, vibration, unusual noises or warning messages. A specialist can help determine whether the cause relates to tyres, drivetrain components or another system.

2. Suspension

Check the ride quality and listen for knocks or unusual noises. If the vehicle has air suspension, look for warning messages, uneven ride height or other signs that the system needs attention.

3. Cooling system and fluid leaks

Ask the inspecting garage to check for coolant loss, oil leaks and evidence of overheating. The relevant components and risks depend on the engine fitted.

4. Electrical systems and infotainment

Test the infotainment display, cameras, parking sensors, powered seats, tailgate and driver-assistance equipment. Intermittent electrical faults can be difficult to assess during a brief viewing, so a diagnostic check is worthwhile.

Audi Q7: What should you inspect?

1. Suspension and ride quality

If the vehicle has adaptive or air suspension, check for warning lights, uneven ride height, unusual noises and changes in handling. Ask a specialist to investigate anything abnormal.

2. Gearbox and drivetrain

During the test drive, check for delayed engagement, harsh shifts, vibration and warning messages. A proper diagnostic inspection may identify issues that are not obvious on a short journey.

3. Diesel emissions equipment

On diesel versions, ask about the vehicle's driving history and maintenance. EGR and diesel particulate filter systems can need attention, particularly where the vehicle's use has not suited the system's operating requirements.

4. Turbocharging and engine management

Investigate poor acceleration, unusual smoke, abnormal noises or engine warning lights. Avoid accepting a seller's assurance that a fault is minor without an appropriate diagnosis.

How much could a major repair cost?

Repair costs depend on the fault, model year, engine, parts, labour rate and diagnostic work. A relatively minor fault may cost far less than replacing a major drivetrain or suspension component, while complex repairs can run into thousands of pounds.

For a useful estimate, ask a garage familiar with the model to provide a written quote. Check whether it includes parts, labour, VAT, diagnostics and any additional work that may be necessary.

This article does not assign a single repair-cost range to either SUV because a generic estimate could be misleading without a specified fault and vehicle configuration.

Before you buy: An independent inspection can help you identify existing issues and negotiate on the basis of evidence, rather than relying solely on a vehicle's service history.

4. BMW X5 vs Audi Q7: Which Is More Reliable?

There is no responsible way to declare every BMW X5 more reliable than every Audi Q7, or vice versa, without comparing specific generations, engines and evidence.

A well-maintained vehicle with a documented history may be a better purchase than a cheaper example with incomplete records or unresolved faults.

To assess a particular used SUV, consider:

  • Service history: Check invoices, maintenance intervals and evidence of previous repairs.
  • MOT history: Review recorded mileage, advisories and failures using the official UK MOT history service.
  • Diagnostic results: Ask a specialist to scan relevant systems and investigate any stored faults.
  • Road-test behaviour: Check the engine, gearbox, steering, brakes and suspension.
  • Previous damage: Verify the vehicle's history and investigate signs of poor-quality repairs.
  • Ownership and usage: Ask how the vehicle was driven, maintained and stored.

You can check a vehicle's MOT history on the official GOV.UK website: https://www.gov.uk/check-mot-history.

An MOT history is useful, but it is not a full mechanical inspection and does not guarantee that a vehicle is free from faults.

Reliability verdict: Choose on the evidence available for the individual vehicle. A specialist inspection, complete service records and a sensible ownership budget are stronger foundations for a decision than broad claims about either brand.

5. Is an Extended Warranty Worth It for a Used BMW X5 or Audi Q7?

Once a manufacturer's warranty has expired, you may have to pay for unexpected repairs yourself unless another form of protection applies.

An extended vehicle warranty can help with the cost of specified mechanical and electrical failures, depending on the policy you choose. It is not the same as motor insurance and does not automatically cover every breakdown, worn component or pre-existing fault.

For a luxury SUV, consider whether the premium and cover limits make sense for your vehicle, budget and tolerance for unexpected costs.

Before buying, check:

  • Eligibility: Is your exact model, engine, age and mileage accepted?
  • Component cover: Are the components you are concerned about included?
  • Claim limits: How much can be paid towards an approved repair?
  • Excess or contribution: Will you have to pay part of the bill?
  • Labour and diagnostics: Are these included, and are limits applicable?
  • Maintenance requirements: What service records and maintenance standards are required?
  • Exclusions: How does the policy treat pre-existing faults, wear and tear, and gradual deterioration?
  • Authorisation: What must you do before a garage starts work?

Read the policy documents rather than relying on a headline price or a general description of cover.

6. Can You Use Your Own Garage for a Warranty Claim?

Garage choice can matter when you own a premium vehicle, especially if you prefer a local specialist familiar with BMW or Audi systems.

BuyA Warranty states that repairs can be carried out by a VAT-registered garage, subject to claim approval and the chosen policy's terms.

The process should be confirmed with the provider before work begins. In general, expect to:

  • Contact the claims team and report the fault.
  • Follow its instructions for diagnosis and documentation.
  • Allow the provider to review the proposed repair against your policy.
  • Obtain authorisation before proceeding with the repair.
  • Confirm what has been approved, including any applicable limit or contribution.

Do not assume that taking the vehicle to a VAT-registered garage automatically guarantees payment. The fault must meet the policy requirements and the claim must be approved.

Read the BuyA Warranty claims information before choosing a plan.

7. What Should You Check Before Buying Either SUV?

Use this checklist when viewing a used BMW X5 or Audi Q7.

  • Verify the registration, mileage and MOT history.
  • Review the service book and repair invoices.
  • Arrange an independent inspection by a garage familiar with the model.
  • Ask for a diagnostic scan and investigate any warning messages.
  • Test the gearbox, steering, brakes and suspension.
  • Check for leaks, smoke, unusual noises and uneven tyre wear.
  • Test the infotainment, cameras, sensors and powered equipment.
  • Confirm the number of seats and the boot space you actually need.
  • Obtain insurance, servicing and tyre estimates.
  • Check the vehicle's eligibility before buying an extended warranty.
  • Read the warranty's exclusions, limits and authorisation requirements.

Do not skip an inspection simply because the vehicle looks clean or has a full service history. Neither guarantees that expensive components are free from faults.

8. BMW X5 vs Audi Q7: Final Verdict

The BMW X5 is a strong option for buyers who value a driver-focused luxury SUV, while the Audi Q7 is worth serious consideration for families who need flexible passenger space.

Your final decision should come down to the exact vehicle's condition, specification, running costs and suitability for your lifestyle.

Before committing, compare service records, arrange an independent inspection and obtain realistic estimates for insurance and maintenance. If unexpected repair bills are a concern, compare extended warranty options and make sure the policy covers the components you want protected.

You can review BuyA Warranty's UK car warranty options to explore available cover. Check your vehicle's eligibility and read the full terms before deciding whether a plan suits your needs.

The best used luxury SUV is not necessarily the one with the most impressive badge. It is the one that meets your needs, has a sound maintenance history and fits your ownership budget.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q1. Is the BMW X5 or Audi Q7 better?

The BMW X5 may suit drivers who prefer a more engaging driving experience, while the Audi Q7 may suit families who need seven-seat flexibility. Compare the specific versions, condition and running costs before deciding.

Q2. Is the Audi Q7 bigger than the BMW X5?

The Q7 is designed around a larger, flexible passenger layout, and selected versions offer seven seats. However, dimensions and usable luggage space vary by model year and configuration. Compare the official specifications for the exact vehicles you are considering.

Q3. Is the BMW X5 expensive to maintain in the UK?

Maintenance costs depend on the engine, age, mileage, condition, parts and labour rates. Obtain a service estimate and arrange an independent inspection to identify potential expenses before buying.

Q4. What should I check when buying a used Audi Q7?

Review the service history and MOT record, test the gearbox and suspension, check the diesel emissions systems where fitted, and test the vehicle's electronics. A specialist inspection can help identify faults that are not obvious during a viewing.

Q5. What are the common repair concerns on a used BMW X5?

Depending on the generation and engine, areas worth inspecting include the drivetrain, suspension, cooling system and electrical equipment. These are inspection priorities, not faults that affect every vehicle.

Q6. Does an extended warranty cover gearbox or suspension repairs?

Some plans cover specified gearbox and suspension components. Whether a particular repair is covered depends on the policy wording, component definitions, exclusions, claim limits and approval process. Confirm the details before purchasing.

Q7. Can I use my own garage with BuyA Warranty?

BuyA Warranty states that repairs can be carried out by a VAT-registered garage, subject to claim approval and the terms of the chosen plan. Contact the claims team before repair work begins.

Q8. Does an extended warranty cover faults that existed before purchase?

Do not assume it does. Pre-existing faults are generally excluded from extended warranty cover. Read the selected policy's wording and confirm any questions with the provider before purchasing.

Q9. How much does a BMW X5 or Audi Q7 extended warranty cost?

The price depends on the vehicle, age, mileage and level of cover. BuyA Warranty cover for a BMW X5 or Audi Q7 starts from £34 a month for 1-year cover (12 monthly instalments, £408 in total), but the actual quote and eligibility depend on the vehicle and chosen plan.
